name: ΑΘΕ
title: Three letters. A civic signature.
text: ΑΘΕ abbreviates “of the Athenians.” The letters are alpha, theta and epsilon. On this coin, theta is a circle with a central dot—the ancient counterpart of the printed Θ.

name: The owl
title: A body in profile. Eyes looking back.
text: The owl’s body turns right while its head faces the viewer.

name: Olive & crescent
title: Small symbols, enduring identity.
text: The olive sprig and crescent accompany the owl on these classical examples. Their presence is observable; a precise commemorative meaning for every detail should not be assumed.

name: The incuse
title: The square belongs to the strike.
text: The reverse sits in a recessed, or incuse, square formed in striking.

name: Athena’s eye
title: The face turns. The eye does not quite follow.
text: The conspicuous almond-shaped eye appears almost frontal although Athena’s face is in profile. Compare it with the fourth-century example farther down the story.

name: The helmet
title: The detail that names a later family.
text: The classical helmet here provides a reference for the changed ornament in the later Pi-style group.
